title: Restic 0.16.3 issue on Windows 7
body:
Edit by @participant2:

# Latest version which works on Windows 7 is [0.16.2](https://github.com/restic/restic/releases/tag/v0.16.2)

### Original issue description
Did the new version of Restic 0.16.3 drop support for Windows 7?

Running 0.16.2 worked fine.  Updated to 0.16.3 with ``restic self-update``:
```
C:\Users\<user>\apps\restic\restic.exe self-update
writing restic to c:\apps\restic\restic.exe
find latest release of restic at GitHub
latest version is 0.16.3
download SHA256SUMS
download SHA256SUMS.asc
GPG signature verification succeeded
download restic_0.16.3_windows_amd64.zip
downloaded restic_0.16.3_windows_amd64.zip
saved 25019392 bytes in c:\apps\restic\restic.exe
successfully updated restic to version 0.16.3
```


After this, all attempts to run restic.exe fail with an error which would appear to be related to compiling issues or dropping support for Windows 7 (which I don't see mentioned in the release notes).

I have manually downloaded the file from the Github release page and attempted to run it, still fails with the following:
```
C:\Users\<user>\apps\restic\restic_0.16.3_windows_amd64.exe version
Exception 0xc0000005 0x8 0x0 0x0
PC=0x0

runtime.asmstdcall()
        /usr/local/go/src/runtime/sys_windows_amd64.s:65 +0x75 fp=0x22fca0 sp=0x
22fc80 pc=0x46d335
rax     0x0
rbx     0x1b5e300
rcx     0x1bb4100
rdi     0x7fffffde000
rsi     0x22fea0
rbp     0x22fde0
rsp     0x22fc78
r8      0x0
r9      0x22fee0
r10     0x1b855b8
r11     0x21
r12     0x22fec0
r13     0x1
r14     0x1b5da60
r15     0x0
rip     0x0
rflags  0x10293
cs      0x33
fs      0x53
gs      0x2b
```
Previous version:
```
C:\Users\<user>\apps\restic\restic.exe version
restic 0.16.2 compiled with go1.21.3 on windows/amd64
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: It's not `restic` but a `go` compiler. You can recompile `restic` with old `go1.21.3` or recompile `go1.21.6` compiler itself, but revert [this](https://<redacted-host>/c/go/+/545355) commit.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: It's somewhat unintended that Windows 7 is no longer supported, although it's not surprising given that Windows 7 has been EOL (the extended EOL deadline!) for more than a year by now. However, as the `go` compiler has dropped support for Windows 7 and does not intend to change that (see https://github.com/golang/go/issues/64622), there's not much we can do. For a limited time you will still be able to compile recent restic versions using an older compiler version, but that will likely also stop working in about 1-2 year.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Thanks for the information.  Unfortunately I do not know much about ``go`` compiling and stuff so I will have to stick with 0.16.2 for now.

comments.author: participant1
participant3
comments.body: try this if you don't want to build it from source every time: https://github.com/participant3/golangwin7patch

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@participant3 unfortunately fixing `ProcessPrng` is not enough: you should fix `exec_windows.go` (need for at least `rclone` backend support) and `dir_windows.go` (need for FAT formatted flash drive support). I think you can achieve this by hooking `CreateProcess` and `GetFileInformationByHandleEx` from you library.
See [this gist](https://gist.github.com/participant1/6e29eb6a8635fae9ab822782f34d8fd6) for details.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: @participant1 thanks! I'm willing to implement this, just need to find a decent hooking library that is public and free. Meanwhile, could you please provide (if possible) a minimal Go test program that fails on Win7 for both cases: https://github.com/participant3/golangwin7patch/issues/1 and https://github.com/participant3/golangwin7patch/issues/2

# Restic 0.18.0 for Windows 7

I installed [patched Go](https://github.com/XTLS/go-win7) 1.23.6 x64 for Windows 7 by @participant10 and compiled Restic 0.18,0.

``` console
$ ver && go version
Microsoft Windows [Version 6.1.7601]
go version go1.23.6 windows/amd64

$ go install -ldflags="-s -w" -tags disable_grpc_modules github.com/restic/restic/cmd/restic@latest

$ restic.exe version
restic 0.18.0 compiled with go1.23.6 on windows/amd64

$ busybox sha256sum restic.exe
c53876bbcfdec3f29d5aa6ec48bb4e2a10441c3afa6a80d817217516e6c6ba7c  restic.exe
```

<mark>Windows 7 x64 users, <mark>grab [restic_v0180_wiin7x64.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19527508/restic_v0180_wiin7x64.zip) if you need it.</mark>

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
@participant5 Look, I get that you are frustrated. Fine. But the restic developers are not responsible for the deprecation of Windows support in Golang (which I recognize is not what you are saying).

I also understand that you feel that as part of the Golang ecosystem, the restic project should put more pressure on the Golang project to make a change in the status quo regarding the Golang project's decision to stop supporting Windows 7. Fine.

But please - the developers of restic does not deserve the words that you just threw at them. They have spent countless days, weeks, months working on this software, year after year. Hence, the way you put forth the criticism is uncalled for.

It is indeed sad that there is no longer any Windows 7 support in current Golang versions, but I kindly ask that you try not to take out the frustration over decisions made in other projects on this project, even if you think more could have been done to affect the outcome.

On a positive note, thanks to someone else's hard work the Golang patches you used can build restic for Windows 7, as you showed above. Your post could have focused more on that, and the splendid instructions you provided in your example above.

Let's all be friends, and try to make the best of things. Sometimes that includes using additional tooling to work around situations originating upstream. Thank you for showing how easy it seems to be to do that.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Re: @participant6

Sweetening communication to the point that you're afraid to stand up is the reason for this mess. Some people live in ignorance of the fact that a person plays multiple roles throughout his or her life. And, of course, they are shocked when suddenly someone reminds them of this, much less rebukes them for not doing well in a particular role. 

One may be a diligent student and an obedient son, but at the same time an unfaithful husband. Likewise, some professional coders here share great programs for free, but they prefer to bury their heads in the sand when they need to prove themselves in a different role — the defender of common sense. And I learned how to write not to be silent about how their polite indifference contributes to suffering and digital segregation.

The role of the defender requires a man to stand up and say: “WTF is going on?” Go team interrupts the relationship between the coder and the users, whose lives the coder is trying to make easier with his program, but the coder is silent. “Well, some of my users are still here”. Where are your balls, man? Buried in the sand as well? Stand up, speak!

We can't stop wars, but we can definitely say NO when Go team releases a compiler that cuts off thousands souls from solutions. If you need Windows 3000 and DirectX100-capable GPU to drive it to launch a Go backup program or even a Go calculator, this is not progress, because you could run a calculator even in DOS on 80286 with 2MB RAM.

It reminds me of the famous [Charlie Chaplin's speech][1] (1940): “…We have developed speed but we have shut ourselves in: machinery that gives abundance has left us in want. Our knowledge has made us cynical, our cleverness hard and unkind. We think too much and feel too little: more than machinery we need humanity…”.

[1]: https://<redacted-host>/watch?v=J7GY1Xg6X20

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant5 As you've already been told in the past, this style of communication is not acceptable. I absolutely don't object to pointing out that some decisions cause problems for certain users, but not in this tone.

> You, active contributors and maintainers with famous names and starred repos, could stand up for your user base.

Even after reading this several times, I'm unsure whether this just takes being direct to the extreme or whether it is a poorly disguised insult. Either way, if you want someone to join your cause this won't help.

> but they prefer to bury their heads in the sand when they need to prove themselves in a different role — the defender of common sense.

"common sense" is not some objective universal criteria. In countries that depend more and more on their IT infrastructure it's becoming common sense to properly secure their systems by keeping them up to date and by replacing or isolating legacy systems. Whether certain operating systems should bump their system requirements as aggressively as they do is a different question though.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@participant7 Unfortunately, your "legacy" build does not work on `Win7`, because your script just downloads original `go1.23`, but not patched `go1.21` (see official docs and [this blog post](https://kokada.dev/blog/quick-bits-go-automatically-downloads-a-newer-toolchain-if-needed/) for details).
But [here](https://gist.github.com/participant1/6e29eb6a8635fae9ab822782f34d8fd6) you can find latest version (`go1.24.2`) of the script.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
@participant1 I actually just followed your old recipe script.
I have a hard time understanding what your current script does. Why do you need go 1.23 __AND__ go 1.24 sources ?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
>Why do you need go 1.23 AND go 1.24 sources ?

You [cannot use](https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.24#bootstrap) `go1.21` for bootstrap `go1.24`.

This script designed to work on `Win7`, if you run it on `Win10/11` you can remove bootstrap from `go1.21` to `go1.23` and even replace `powershell` and `wget` by `curl` (supported since `Win10` build 17063).

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
Well, someone at my work with better Go Skills(TM) than mine has pointed out that using go1.21 to build go1.23 to build go1.25 is only necessary if you plan to build from Windows 7.
Hence, I've modified my restic builder script in https://github.com/netinvent/npbackup/blob/main/RESTIC_SOURCE_FILES/legacy_restic_builder.cmd to just download latest go1.25 compiler and make restic binaries for Win7.
This should obviously speed up compilation by an order of magnitude.
Of course, the script needs to run on Windows 10 or better.

Yet, another solution he has pointed out is to build on any linux with target Windows 7 since go does cross compiling.
Here's another script for linux: https://github.com/netinvent/npbackup/blob/main/RESTIC_SOURCE_FILES/legacy_restic_builder.sh

Both scripts do build byte identical restic versions.
I'll keep restic legacy builds uptodate as long as I can support Windows 7 in my project at https://github.com/netinvent/npbackup/tree/main/RESTIC_SOURCE_FILES
